questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good university in a beautiful location. The language taught and the reputation of the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can really recommend doing an exchange on UBC. The only downside was that we were 40+ Danish students, which has its pros and cons, but something you have to consider if you chose to take an exchange at UBC in a fall semester.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find the right information about the courses on the host universitys homepage. KU was helpful when I needed information before going there. After arrival they responded really fast when I needed it (something about my course registration), which was very important for my stay there (because I ended up with the courses I wanted).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to UBC's study abroad office a couple of time for help and information. And as mentioned above, I got help with the preapprovals after arriving, because I changed some courses during the first two weeks of the term.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living in a dorm with five other exchange students, which was one of the best things of my exchange.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I was offered something but said no, because it was expensive, and I wanted to cook my own food.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a great way to get to know other exchange students, and get a "social circle" while being very far from home, which is amazing. Your roommates are probably quite a bit younger than you, but my experience was that it was okay, since you are all there for the same reason, and want to experience the city/surroundings. The room is not very personal, so bring something to decorate your room with. I printed pictures of friends and family to put on the wall, but overall it still felt as a quite "institutional" room/apartment.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Most of it is done through KU, but finding the courses was the most difficult part because you have to look through the old course list and figure out which courses you are allowed to take, be aware of not taking courses that have lectures at the same time, etc. It was divided in several steps - back in DK, I had to make a list of ten prioritised courses, which felt like a waste of time, because I wasn't sure that I would get them and ten courses is a lot, when you only have to take three (as a
postgrad.pol.sci
.-student), and then in August I had write to the professors to get a signature that I could take their course, and that has to be done quite early in August (or mid August) because the courses get full, and then you are not sure to get a spot. But again the professors were quite fast at responding, whenever you contact them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could write to UBC's Global Contact, and then they would respond within a couple of days.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It took some time, but I ended up getting the courses, I hoped for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were some really interesting courses that was shifted from Term 1 to Term 2, which was super frustrating.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were overall more demanding throughout the semester than I'm used to from KU. But once I got into the habit of it, I really enjoyed that way of teaching, because the courses I took were quite small and the professors actually knew our names and was interested in getting to know us and our academic interest, which I ended up enjoying a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above it is way more active way of taking classes, you have to participate in the courses (your participation is graded), you have to hand in assignments weekly or monthly, and I also had to host a full three hour class with one of my co-students. It can feel a bit stressfull in the beginning because it is quite different from UCPH, but I ended up enjoying it a lot because I learned way more about the subjects and became more confident in the subjects.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Policy Responses to Global Climate Change (with Milind Kandlikar)
Topics in Canadian Politics: Urban Governance and Policy in Canada (with Carey Doberstein)
Survey Design in Environmental Social Sciences (with Terre Satterfield)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I believe that any courses with Carey Doberstein and Terre Satterfield would be great. They were really good professors and the courses I took with them was good.
Milind Kandlikar is great as well but a bit more unstructured. His course was great because it is a cross-disciplinary course so the students had all different kind of academic backgrounds, which made the class really interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Canada is really expensive, so make sure to have savings when you go there, because there is a lot of great opportunities to participate in, but it is expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I went on trips almost every weekend, and that was expensive, but worth all the money.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot. UBC has a broad range of opportunities and they are all great, so make sure to enroll in something when you get there. There is so many opportunities so it is a help to have an idea of what you want to enroll in, when you get there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Varsity Outdoor Club (VOC), they arrange great trips and you can rent outdoor gear from them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the mountains as much as possible. Sign up for the VOC trips. Make an account on EVO, which is a car sharing opportunity that is great if you don't want to buy your own car.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, UBC are very inclusive and used to hosting international students, so you won't feel as the only non-Canadian. I mostly connected with other exchange students but made a couple of Canadian friends as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Use the opportunities on campus to drink coffee, take a walk, do a quiz or something like that with the other students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Being nuanced in expressing myself. It can be frustrating but also one of the good challenges of being on exchange.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The very easily accessible outdoor opportunities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Apply for housing on campus (it is difficult to find housing off campus since there is a housing crisis in Vancouver), make sure to enjoy all the great non-academic opportunities that UBC offers, and enjoy the nature around Vancouver/British Columbia.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Things will sort out, and you will meet a lot of nice exchange students who are struggling with the same things as you, and who are also up for making the most of your time abroad.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Taking part in an international community

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping in touch with friends and family back home because of the time difference (9 hours)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
